original_question: For the infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian with short-range or finite-range interaction considered in the paper, namely a system of the form H = sum_{j in Z^d} omega_j I_j + epsilon sum_{<i,j>} f_{i,j}(I_i, I_j; phi_i, phi_j), where the perturbation is short range or finite range and the frequencies are weakly correlated, KAM tori are constructed when the initial actions are strongly localized or even decay weaker than exponentially. Does there also exist an infinite-dimensional KAM torus when the initial actions decay only polynomially, in the sense that the action profile satisfies epsilon_j = I_j^0 approximately |j|^{-M} for some sufficiently large M > 0?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 1.2: the open problem asking whether there are any infinite-dimensional KAM tori for initial conditions with polynomial decay ε_j = I_j^0 ≈ |j|^{-M}, with some large M > 0, for the Section 1 Hamiltonian (1.1) under the same short-range/finite-range and weak-correlation hypotheses used there. ([cdn.sciengine.com](https://cdn.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/df39fa9b911c46db9c3ce2d6abaff89b))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the Section 1 Hamiltonian class, the short-range or finite-range interaction assumption, the weak correlation of the frequencies, the comparison with previously known exponentially or weaker-than-exponentially decaying action profiles, and the central polynomial-decay existence question. It is clearly aimed at the infinite-dimensional KAM-torus open problem in Section 1 rather than the later finite-dimensional results. ([cdn.sciengine.com](https://cdn.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/df39fa9b911c46db9c3ce2d6abaff89b))
missing_details: The paper states this as an open problem labeled Problem 1.2, not as a theorem or conjecture already proved in the paper. ([cdn.sciengine.com](https://cdn.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/df39fa9b911c46db9c3ce2d6abaff89b))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should restore the ambient hypotheses from equations (1.1)–(1.4): j ranges over Z^d, the symplectic form is sum_j dI_j ∧ dφ_j, the interaction term f_{<i,j>} is analytic on some domain and is O(I^2), and the frequencies ω_j are weakly correlated, for example i.i.d. with a smooth positive distribution. ([cdn.sciengine.com](https://cdn.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/df39fa9b911c46db9c3ce2d6abaff89b))

The official context compares the polynomial-decay question with two earlier action profiles: the Theorem 1.1 regime I_j^0 = exp(-|j|^{d+α}) with α > 0, and the weaker restriction later suggested by Pöschel, ε_j ≈ exp(-(log |j|)^{1+α}). Those benchmarks help pin down the exact intent of the open problem. ([cdn.sciengine.com](https://cdn.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/df39fa9b911c46db9c3ce2d6abaff89b))

The paper's wording is specifically ε_j = I_j^0 ≈ |j|^{-M} with some large M > 0. It does not formalize the asymptotic symbol ≈ or quantify large any further, so a faithful rewrite should not silently strengthen this to a sharper unsupported quantifier. ([cdn.sciengine.com](https://cdn.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/df39fa9b911c46db9c3ce2d6abaff89b))

No algebraic ambient field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition is part of this problem; the hidden assumptions are analytic and dynamical instead. ([cdn.sciengine.com](https://cdn.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/df39fa9b911c46db9c3ce2d6abaff89b))

The target is the infinite-dimensional KAM-torus problem attached to the Section 1 model (1.1), not the finite-dimensional short-range KAM/breather theory beginning in Section 2. ([cdn.sciengine.com](https://cdn.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/df39fa9b911c46db9c3ce2d6abaff89b))
refined_question: For the infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian H = sum_{j∈Z^d} ω_j I_j + ε sum_{<i,j>} f_{<i,j>}(I_i, I_j; φ_i, φ_j), equipped with the symplectic structure sum_j dI_j ∧ dφ_j, where the perturbation f_{<i,j>} is analytic and O(I^2), is either short range in the sense |f_{<i,j>}| ≤ C e^{-m|i-j|} for some m > 0 or finite range in the sense f_{<i,j>} = 0 for |i-j| > ρ̃, and where the frequencies ω_j are weakly correlated (for example i.i.d. with a smooth distribution), does there exist any infinite-dimensional invariant KAM torus for initial actions I^0 = (I_j^0)_{j∈Z^d} ∈ R_+^{Z^d} having only polynomial decay, namely I_j^0 = ε_j ≈ |j|^{-M} for some large M > 0? ([cdn.sciengine.com](https://cdn.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/df39fa9b911c46db9c3ce2d6abaff89b))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's actual intent. In Section 1, after stating Theorem 1.1 for strongly localized actions and then mentioning Pöschel's weaker subexponential profile, the paper explicitly formulates Problem 1.2 as the polynomial-decay question ε_j = I_j^0 ≈ |j|^{-M} with some large M > 0. The refinement above therefore keeps the question narrow, restores only the standing hypotheses from equations (1.1)–(1.4), and avoids adding stronger quantifiers or variants not present in the paper. ([cdn.sciengine.com](https://cdn.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/df39fa9b911c46db9c3ce2d6abaff89b))
